pr_body: Fixes #82794. Upgrade the Spotless plugin, which addresses the issue around formatting `instanceof` expressions. Formatting of statements including lambdas seems to have improved too.
pr_comments:
> Still, I'm pretty sure we could debate this stuff all day.

Indeed. I have the exact opposite preference and we'll likely never completely reach a consensus. The point is to just eliminate the debate by enforcing this and forcing people to deal with it 😉

issue_context.title: Spotless removes space before `instanceof` in pattern match
comments:
This looks to be a bug in eclipse-jdt. There's no explicit formatter setting for `instanceof` pattern matching, it's just the formatter not understanding this syntax. Eclipse version 2021.12, using eclipse-jdt 4.22 works as intended. We unfortunately have to wait for a) the IntelliJ plugin to update the bundled Eclipse libraries and b) Spotless to update eclipse-jdt to 4.22.

I was able to get the IDE to work as intended by configuring the IntelliJ Eclipse Formatter plugin to point to an Eclipse 2021.12 installation, so that at least confirms that version of eclipse-jdt works as intended. That said, we need both IDE and CLI to match otherwise folks will reformat in IntelliJ and spotless with complain or vice versa.

We can open a PR for spotless for this but the [IntelliJ plugin](https://github.com/krasa/EclipseCodeFormatter) doesn't seem to use any kind of dependency management. I suspect the author has to download the updated libraries locally and rebuild.
We aren't the only ones asking for this: https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/issues/1059

> An aesthetic thing for sure but I think it's better with the space than without.

This definitely triggers me as well.
Spotless has finally updated, so we should now be able to address this issue.

review_comments:
I'm wondering if we can have it reformat these single-line lambdas as expressions instead of code blocks so it doesn't try to turn a single-line statement into a multi-line one. For example, this should just be:

```java
(handler, request, channel, task) -> logger.info("drop the check shards request")
```

The Eclipse formatter doesn't support these kinds of structural changes, it's just a formatter.

Spotless does now appear to support an additional tool called [cleanthat](https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/tree/main/plugin-gradle#cleanthat), which can do automated refactorings (see also the [homepage](https://github.com/solven-eu/cleanthat)). Unfortunately when I tried it, I got some weird dependency conflict error, and decided not to investigate further. I'll leave that to you 😁 I did get IntelliJ to look for all potential fix sites, and there's just over 1000. Also, making the change to remove lambda blocks doesn't always result in more readable code after a format. It needs more investigation 🤷 

I do indeed intend to update `.git-blame-ignore-revs` after merging.
